validator: one soft problem: summary.rule is 700 characters (keep under 600); otherwise passes

faults.finding: Screen 2 says an electrical tree 'starts at' a bad defect without saying why the overvoltage finds it: at the test voltage a big enough defect is excited and discharges inside, and those discharges start the tree. Screen 4 says halving the frequency lets the set drive twice the capacitance without the step between: the set can only supply so much current. 'Lowering the frequency needlessly is to be avoided' is given with no reason, though the recommended times are set at 0.1 Hz.
faults.fix: Add the partial discharge step on screen 2 and in explain para 1. Add 'the set can only supply so much current' on screen 4, and that the recommended times are given at 0.1 Hz.

faults.finding: 'Smaller defects are not affected' keeps the source's qualifier, and 'a high chance' keeps the notes'. 'DC needs almost no current' keeps its 'almost'. 'That has been found to speed up water trees' is a passive report of one study, worded as a finding. No other absolutes.
faults.fix: Say 'That can speed up water trees in healthy XLPE.'

faults.finding: Screen 3 draws the cause, the number of cycles in the same 10 s, beside the current bar it drives, so the 500 times shows as 500 cycles against one. Screen 4 draws the core's capacitance growing with length against the set's rating at each frequency, the cause of a long cable needing a lower frequency. Passes.
The check asks what halving the frequency does to the current. It needs the reactance reasoning, not the rule's words, and each wrong answer names the reversed or missing step. Passes.

The contested range is taught with both views and the client's spec settles it; the resonant 10 to 500 Hz test for a 66 kV cable is taught as a spec that may apply.
faults.fix: Drop [^19]; keep seven, each on a figure or rule he would look up on a job.

faults.fix: Say 'despite L2's failed sheath test'. Trim the card's notes: drop the kVA line and fold the discharge order into the traps.
